newsitem.title: ITALY: Magistrates to quiz Olivetti's Caio on accounts.
newsitem.headline: Magistrates to quiz Olivetti's Caio on accounts.

text.p: Olivetti's embattled chief executive Francesco Caio is to be questioned by magistrates in the group's home town of Ivrea in a preliminary probe into the company's accounts, judicial sources said on Monday.

Caio will come under investigation by magistrates in a first step which could lead to a full-scale criminal inquiry into public statements made by the loss-making information technology group on its finances.

Magistrates, who launched their inquiry at the weekend, have questioned former Olivetti director-general in charge of finance and auditing, Renzo Francesconi, after he cast doubts on the accuracy of the group's first half financial accounts.
Shares in Olivetti on Monday slumped to a fresh record low of 516 lire and were suspended automatically after hitting the Milan bourse fluctuation limit of 10 percent.

Olivetti stock began to slide earlier in the day after the group cancelled an anxiously awaited analysts' meeting this week and delayed the publication of its fully detailed first-half 1996 results until the end of the month.

Late on Friday, Olivetti called off the analysts meeting in Milan on Monday and London on Tuesday as the crisis-hit group attempted to satisfy an earlier investigation by stock market watchdog Consob over its accounts.

Earlier this month, Olivetti reported initial first half 1996 results showing sales sliding, losses continuing and debts deepening. Francesconi resigned a day later after he questioned the validity of the group's figures.

Financial analysts said the group must produce a full set of approved accounts before the process of re-building confidence in the group can start. Market talk that the group's debts were worse than reported had already prompted selling of the shares.
